summary.headline: Jeena Sikho Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29% YoY to INR224 crore, with EBITDA of INR92 crore (41% margin) and PAT of INR65 crore (28%).
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of INR224 crore (up 29% YoY), EBITDA of INR92 crore (up 17% YoY, 41% margin) and PAT of INR65 crore. Government hospital business was cut sharply (INR15 crore to INR5 crore YoY per management), while private Panchakarma and product sales grew. Management attributed part of the cost base to one-off items: about INR4 crore extra advertising, about INR2 crore software implementation and audit fees. Other income of INR14 crore included about INR7 crore one-time gains (warrant valuation and capital gain), per the CFO. Management guided to 30% annual growth and INR3,000 crore turnover within about 3 to 5 years, but gave no quantified FY27 guidance beyond 3,000 to 3,500 operational beds.

financial_highlights.change: +29% YoY (INR174 crore in Q1 FY26); QoQ growth stated as about 10% on patient/volume basis
Q1 FY27 PAT of INR51 crore was also cited by an analyst and management in the Q&A; treat PAT figure as inconsistent in transcript
Up from INR4 crore in Q4 FY26; about INR7 crore one-time (INR5 crore warrant valuation, INR2.5 crore capital gain)
Panchakarma revenue +13% YoY; private Panchakarma INR78 crore to INR100 crore (about 30% YoY)
Products business grew 47% YoY; INR80 crore in Q1 FY26 per management comparison
Down from INR15 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR15 crore in prior-year Q1 per management

segments.name: Ayurveda healthcare services (Panchakarma, hospitals)
segments.commentary: Panchakarma revenue +13% YoY; IPD patients +33% YoY (about 8,600 to 11,500) and day care volume +31% YoY (day care per-day volume 16,000 to 19,000 per management). Government revenue cut to INR5 crore from INR15 crore as management exited credit-heavy government business.

segments.name: Ayurveda products
segments.commentary: Products grew 47% YoY; medicine sales INR118 crore in Q1, flat vs Q4 FY26. E-commerce orders rose to 2,64,000 from 2,28,000 QoQ; COD patients rose to 18,500 from 14,000.

segments.name: Ultra-luxury wellness (Manali, Jeena Sikho Premium)
segments.commentary: Pre-launch; 108 rooms plus 22 villas, guaranteed 35 rooms under a 3-year lease renewable 3+3+3. Management expects little FY27 contribution, with launch around Sep-Oct 2026 and better season from March; guided year-one EBITDA 35-40%+ and year-two 60% occupancy at ADR INR35,000-37,000.

guidance_outlook: Target of 30% YoY growth annually and INR3,000 crore turnover in about 3 years (maximum 5 years); INR1,000 crore PAT ambition over the longer term.
Operational beds to rise from 2,400 to 3,000-3,500 in FY27; 7,000-10,000 beds targeted in 3-5 years; occupancy target 75-80%.
Plans for 3-4 more luxury wellness centres in India, each guided at INR3-5 crore net profit (management).

Ayushman Bharat/insurance claim inclusion for Ayurveda expected but timing unclear (2-6 months per management); discounted admissions for BPL and Ayushman patients to begin within about 10 days, with 500 beds mentioned.
Entero OTC product listings expected to start across its distributors within about 15 days.
capex_capacity: Operational beds 2,400 as of Q1 FY27, up 100 in the quarter; bed occupancy 59% on 2,400 beds per management.
Panvel hospital currently 49 beds pending OC/fire approvals; to scale to 250 beds, which management says could multiply its revenue 4-5x.
Manali luxury wellness centre: launch around Sep-Oct 2026 after Himachal Pradesh NOC process; 108 rooms and 22 villas, 35 rooms guaranteed under lease.
Management said about INR15 crore revenue from a single Meerut centre.
demand_pricing: Management says patient ecosystem touchpoints rose to 5,34,000 from 4,87,000 QoQ (about 10%); OPD about 1.5 lakh; IPD 10,900 to 11,500 QoQ.
Consultation/COD/OPD-linked patients up 143% YoY and VOPD consultations up 65% YoY per management.
Ticket size fell as discounted admissions were introduced for lower-income patients; management said realisation per patient will be lower on the discount segment.
Government business deliberately shrunk because of receivable risk; management says it will re-engage only once NHA panel payments are reliable (3-6 months).
Advertising expense up about INR4 crore YoY tied to TV integrations (Colors TV shows, Khatron Ke Khiladi), with benefits expected in subsequent quarters; ad budget up 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue flat QoQ and what is the advertising cost run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said QoQ patient/volume growth was about 10% and government business was cut to one-third; advertising was up INR4 crore in Q1 with benefits expected in later quarters under a 6-month TV tie-up.

qa_highlights.question: Why do IPD (+33%) and OPD (+22%) volume growth not translate into similar revenue growth (+11-13%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the government-business decline (INR10 crore drop), discounted pricing for lower-income patients, and a lag in OPD-to-Panchakarma conversion; the CFO said incremental ticket size has fallen.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 other income (INR14 crore) is one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR7 crore is one-time (INR5 crore warrant valuation, INR2.5 crore capital gain); recurring other income about INR4-5 crore plus treasury/FD income.

qa_highlights.question: What are the one-off costs in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly INR4 crore extra advertising, about INR2 crore software implementation instalment, and about INR0.5 crore extra audit fees; management said these expenses will continue.

qa_highlights.question: Manali luxury wellness economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 35 rooms guaranteed under a 3-year lease; year-one occupancy 50% at ADR INR32,000-35,000, year-two 60% at ADR INR35,000-37,000, with 35-40%+ EBITDA in year one. Minimal operating cost since the lessor bears utilities and most staff costs.

qa_highlights.question: Pet Shuddhi price gap versus Pet Saffa?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its manufacturing cost is about four times the competitor, citing a multi-shot formulation and liver/spleen/metabolism claims.

risks_watch: Other income quality: about INR7 crore of the INR14 crore Q1 other income is one-time (warrant valuation and capital gain); recurring base is about INR4-5 crore plus treasury income, so Q1 PAT is flattered.

Government business reduced to INR5 crore from INR15 crore; management says re-engagement only after NHA panel payments are reliable (3-6 months), so the services revenue mix and receivable risk need tracking.

Discounted admissions for BPL and Ayushman patients start within about 10 days at INR4,000-6,000 realisation, which will dilute ticket size; the Ayushman Bharat insurance inclusion timing is unclear (2-6 months).
Recurring one-off-type costs: management said the INR4 crore extra advertising, INR2 crore software instalment and audit fees will continue, so margin sustainability at 41% needs checking.

Execution milestones: Entero OTC listings expected within about 15 days; Manali luxury centre launch around Sep-Oct 2026 pending Himachal NOCs, with little FY27 contribution; Panvel moving from 49 to 250 beds pending OC and fire approvals.
Q2 run-rate needed for 30% growth implies a step-up from the Q1 base; management gave no quantified FY27 revenue or PAT guidance beyond 3,000-3,500 operational beds.
key_quotes: Please don't judge us quarter-on-quarter. If you look at our patient count and volume, overall quarter-on-quarter growth is 10%.
So that INR10 crores decline in hospital business is not a drop in operational business; I deliberately shut down credit business.
So, in quarter 1, it was INR15 crores and this quarter 1, it is INR5 crores.
So, the one-time other income we have booked is around INR7 crores, in which around INR5 crores is warrant valuation and INR2.5 crores is capital gain income.
Sir, this will continue to happen. Our main aim is to take the benefit of our operating leverage.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and expansive on the long-term vision (INR3,000 crore turnover, 7,000-10,000 beds, prevention model) but was defensive and deflecting on quarter-on-quarter revenue flatness and on the gap between IPD/OPD volume growth and revenue growth, repeatedly asking analysts to judge on a yearly basis. Answers on one-off costs and other income were more specific, with the CFO quantifying items, while Manali economics and Ayushman timing were presented with optimism but few hard dates.

adds.what: Operational beds to rise from 2,400 to 3,000-3,500 in FY27
Panvel hospital scale-up to 250 beds from 49 beds, pending OC/fire approvals
Manali ultra-luxury wellness centre, 108 rooms plus 22 villas (35 rooms guaranteed under lease)
3-4 more luxury wellness centres in India, each guided at INR3-5 crore net profit

growth.why: Management reiterated about 30% annual growth and 3,000-3,500 operational beds in FY27 (from 2,400), with Manali luxury centre launching Sep-Oct 2026, but occupancy is only 59% and the Manali contribution in FY27 is expected to be small, and the 30% target is a multi-year ambition rather than a quantified FY27 guide.
